definitions.explanation: A common weed with yellow flowers that turn into white fluffy seed heads.

examples.japanese: ⟦{黄色|きいろ}い→黄色い：00959_kiiroi⟧たんぽぽ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧。
⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たんぽぽ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many dandelions in the park.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たんぽぽ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{生|は}えている→生える：02392_haeru⟧。
examples.english: Many dandelions are growing in the garden.
When you blow dandelion fluff, it floats away on the wind.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なると→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦あちこち→あちこち：01687_achikochi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たんぽぽ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}いて→咲く：08150_saku⟧、⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦たち→たち：01551_tachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦うれしそうに→うれしい：00822_ureshii⟧⟦{摘|つ}んでいる→摘む：02472_tsumu⟧。
examples.english: When spring comes, dandelions bloom everywhere along the road, and children happily pick them.

notes:
たんぽぽ is the Japanese word for dandelion, a common spring flower.

WRITING:
Can be written as {蒲公英|たんぽぽ}, but hiragana is far more common in everyday use.

PARTS OF THE PLANT:
- ⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧: the yellow flower
- ⟦{綿毛|わたげ}→綿毛：20021_watage⟧: the fluffy white seed head
- ⟦{茎|くき}→茎：14119_kuki⟧: stem
- ⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: leaves (jagged, edible)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- たんぽぽ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}く→咲く：08150_saku⟧: dandelions bloom
- たんぽぽ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{綿毛|わたげ}→綿毛：20021_watage⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧: to blow dandelion seeds

CULTURAL NOTE:
Blowing dandelion seeds (⟦{綿毛|わたげ}→綿毛：20021_watage⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飛|と}ばす→飛ばす：02373_tobasu⟧) while making a wish is a popular childhood activity in Japan, similar to Western cultures.

FUNCTIONS:
Dandelion leaves and roots are used in some traditional medicines and herbal teas (たんぽぽ⟦{茶|ちゃ}→茶：03433_cha⟧/⟦コーヒー→コーヒー：00789_koohii⟧).
